record.original_question: For 0 < beta < 1 and q = d/(d-beta), a known result proves that if f is radial and belongs to W^{1,1}(R^d), then the uncentered fractional maximal function is weakly differentiable and satisfies ||∇M̃_beta f||_{L^q(R^d)} <= C ||∇f||_{L^1(R^d)}. Does the analogous statement hold for the centered fractional maximal operator M_beta acting on radial functions?

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.3 (Luiro and Madrid, 2017 - cf. [29]). Given 0 < β < 1 and q = d/(d − β), there is a constant C = C(d, β) such that for every radial function f ∈ W 1,1 (Rd) we have that the uncentered fractional maximal operator is weakly differentiable and ||∇M̃β f||_{Lq(Rd)} ≤ C ||∇f||_{L1(Rd)}.
Question 8. Does Theorem 5.3 hold for the centered fractional maximal operator Mβ acting on radial functions f?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\geq 2$ and $0<\beta<1$. For a locally integrable function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$, define the centered fractional Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator by
$$M_\beta f(x) \;=\; \sup_{r>0}\, r^{\beta}\, \frac{1}{|B(x,r)|}\int_{B(x,r)} |f(y)|\,dy,$$
where $B(x,r)$ is the open Euclidean ball of radius $r$ centered at $x$. A function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ is called radial if $f(x)$ depends only on $|x|$. Set $q=d/(d-\beta)$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $C=C(d,\beta)$ such that, for every radial function $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the function $M_\beta f$ is weakly differentiable on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and satisfies
$$\|\nabla M_\beta f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)} \;\leq\; C\,\|\nabla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}.$$
artifact.category_tag: Endpoint Sobolev regularity of maximal operators
artifact.status_search_result: D. Beltran and J. Madrid, "Regularity of the centered fractional maximal function on radial functions" (Journal of Functional Analysis 279 (2020), no. 8, 108686), establish that for radial $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $q=d/(d-\beta)$, the map $f\mapsto |\nabla M_\beta f|$ is bounded (and continuous) from $W^{1,1}$ to $L^q$, thereby answering the question affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of the centered fractional maximal function on radial functions
status_evidence.snippet: Beltran and Madrid prove that the map f↦|∇M_β f| is bounded and continuous from W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^q(R^d) in the endpoint case q=d/(d−β) for radial functions.
status_evidence.claim: The centered analogue of the endpoint Sobolev bound for the fractional maximal operator on radial W^{1,1} functions is established.
